visual.general_description: Process schematic mapping six steps from awareness to cancer care against three patient-case lines that each meet an ECHO session label.
visual.detailed_description: Colour process schematic on a white page with a purple bar along the bottom edge. The left column has a grey header "Process: Presentation to the start of cancer treatment" above six dark-blue rounded boxes numbered 1 to 6 and joined by a grey vertical line: 1 Awareness (The health care provider has awareness of cancer), 2 Testing (Diagnostic labs and imaging are obtained), 3 Supportive care (Appropriate management to stabilize oncologic emergencies), 4 Diagnosis (A confirmatory diagnosis for suspected malignancy is obtained), 5 Referral (Transfer to appropriate health care facility to begin cancer treatment) and 6 Cancer care (Patient is at a specialized center to begin directed cancer therapy). The right column has a grey header "Patient cases from ECHO sessions" with three vertical lines, one per case. Each line starts as a teal line, carries a printed label "Case 1", "Case 2" or "Case 3" followed by a teal arrowhead pointing down to the words "ECHO session", and the Case 1 and Case 2 lines continue below the ECHO session label as orange-red arrows pointing down to the level of box 6. The Case 1 label sits beside box 1, the Case 2 label beside box 4 and the Case 3 label beside box 6; the Case 3 line has no orange-red arrow below its ECHO session label. No patient measurements, dates or identifier text are printed.

clinical_significance.statement: The authors cite the figure to illustrate how, across the three patients, spoke-site decision making before the ECHO session moved from uncertainty in diagnostic evaluation to appropriate tests and emergent transfer.

evidence.quote: the first patient highlighted uncertainty in which diagnostic evaluations were performed, the second patient exhibited correct diagnostic evaluation but uncertainty in next steps in management, and the final patient demonstrated appropriate diagnostic tests which facilitated emergent patient transfer before the session (Fig 1)
